text:
riley: heads-up — after the L7 tighten in eu3 this morning we're seeing a cluster of staging GPU nodes (~30) stuck at JOIN_PENDING. Keystore-proxy reports 502/504s, KMS decrypt p95 ~10s, and auditlog exporter is retrying like crazy. Anyone on infra notice natgw conntrack high?
oncall-bot: [ALERT] keystore-proxy.decrypt_timeouts eu3 - severity: high - 2026-03-24T07:42:11Z
jenn: yep, conntrack on natgw-c spiked to 97%. lots of TCP_RETRANS and short-lived TLS handshakes failing. DPI in the new FW policy seems to be reassembling TLS sessions — that reassembly doesn't play nicely with ephemeral provisioning flows.
matt: confirmed in packet captures — SACKs + retransmits to 172.31.30.0/24. audit-sink backlog increased x13 and is causing downstream S3 exporter POST storms.
lucas: compliance required default-deny at L7, so we can't revert globally. Proposed short-term: scoped exception that allows provisioning-subnet -> keystore-proxy:443 with an IAM condition binding source-role=arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/provisioner and source-vpc=vpc-eu3-provision. Also enable audit sampling 5-10% for bootstrap traffic.
riley: good. keep exception window short (<=90m). we need postmortem numbers later. jenn can you also escalate conntrack capacity in the short term?
jenn: applied quick mitigation in eu3: 1) added SG exception for prov-subnet -> keystore-proxy:443 2) bumped conntrack limits on natgw hosts 3) enabled audit sampling 10% for tag:onboarding
jen: commands I ran on natgw-hosts:
```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=280000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=35000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=360000
# restart exporter agent after conntrack bump
sudo systemctl restart audit-exporter.service```
matt: after the SG exception we saw first successful joins — KMS decrypt p50 ~150ms, p95 ~700ms, conntrack down to 62%. Audit sink error rate dropped significantly.
lucas: I'll open a short-lived sec-exception ticket sec-exc-4372 and draft ACL PR that scopes by role + port + tag. Also adding keystore response-cache (local ttl 25s) for bootstrap flows to cut decrypt QPS.
finance-bot: Notice: increasing conntrack and allowing cross-VPC exceptions may increase logging/egress. rough estimate: migrating 30 staging joins to us-west-2 warmpool for 60m ~ $60 (egress + image pulls) vs potential wasted GPU prewarm ~ $400.
riley: go ahead with cross-region warm pool for noncritical staging while we fix. matt, tag nodes staging-move.
matt: starting migration of non-critical jobs to us-west-2 warmpool, nodes tagged 'staging-move'. leaving a snippet for scoped SG + IAM condition I'll put in the PR:
```# SG exception (example)
- type: deny
  src: 10.240.50.0/24
  dst: 172.31.30.0/24:443
+ type: allow
  src: 10.240.50.0/24
  dst: 172.31.30.0/24:443
  condition:
    aws:SourceArn: arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/provisioner
    aws:SourceVpc: vpc-eu3-provision
  ttl: 90m
```
riley: keep a strict audit trail — tag all temporary rules with "temp:keystore-exc" and add who/when. we'll revoke after PR merge.
oncall-bot: Incident logged: INC-20260324-11 - eu3 keystore/dpi causing conntrack/auditlog backpressure. Assigned: riley, jenn, lucas.
lucas: PR opened for ACL + IAM condition, will also include automated revoke after 60m. planning to add a runbook note: if you see TCP_RETRANS + high SACKs to keystore IPs + audit sink retries, check FW DPI and conntrack.
matt: quick debug tip: to reproduce locally, use a short-lived TLS client that connects/disconnects rapidly — DPI reassembly tends to hold state and causes retransmits. also watch nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_* values.
riley: ok, once PR is merged we shrink the exception window to 30m and schedule postmortem. include metrics: joins delayed, keystore decrypt latencies, audit exporter retry count, conntrack peaks, and cost delta. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
